Hvidovre Hospital is a Danish healthcare organization recognized for its exceptional performance in acute surgery outcomes. Within the national quality development strategy for acute surgery, evaluated in the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) report, Hvidovre Hospital is distinguished for its sustained success in reducing patient mortality [^src1]. 

The hospital is specifically identified as a "best practice" unit alongside Herlev Hospital for achieving exceptionally good longitudinal results regarding mortality [^src1]. This recognition is directly tied to [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]], a key clinical quality indicator that measures 30-day mortality following acute surgical interventions [^src1]. By maintaining these outstanding results over time, Hvidovre Hospital serves as a critical benchmark for other medical units, driving national knowledge sharing and compliance efforts aimed at improving surgical survival rates across the country [^src1].
